purpose: Can I operate at the speed of thought? Living design inventory, not a promise of implementation.

priority.P0: Strong first-week utility or a prerequisite; estimated, not measured
priority.P1: High-value compositional extension after its prerequisites
priority.P2: Conditional or lower-frequency; do not build without observed demand

status.user_observed: User reports this exact baseline works
status.documented: Platform capability documented; target flow not tested
status.existing_precedent: Existing project demonstrates a useful pattern; new flow untested

design_rules.maintenance: Append or refine stable IDs in this canonical file. Consolidate overlapping intentions; change priority with observed use; promote only on actual evidence. Keep rare operations discoverable without placing them on the main surface. Record a concrete failure and decision when abandoning a branch. No telemetry or persistent personal captures in this public repo.
design_rules.week_review: After seven days of real use, compare frequency, interactions avoided, interruptions, rediscovery without docs, failures and whether the result advanced a real goal. Review after one month too. No invented scores or usage counts.
design_rules.public_privacy: This public atlas is design metadata only, not a screenshot archive, task log, credential store or personal research inbox.

capabilities.name: Screenshot
capabilities.why: Existing double-tap AssistiveTouch gesture is an already-internalized baseline; preserve it.
mechanisms: AssistiveTouch double tap
optional voice command or separate Shortcut for processing
capabilities.acceptance: Existing double tap captures the intended screen without navigating away; no regression.
capabilities.week_later: Keep the existing gesture unchanged; measure new routes against it.
capabilities.boundary: User reports the gesture works; automated routing and continuous capture are not established.

capabilities.name: Ask about what I see
capabilities.why: Visual context is essential for figures, equations, UI state, remote desktops and bugs; avoids explaining what is already visible.
mechanisms: Screenshot share sheet or Take Screenshot action; choose image; attach to supported AI app; OCR only when text is needed
Optional explicit crop/redaction
capabilities.acceptance: From a real Kami diagram and remote desktop error, deliver the intended image plus one dictated question to an AI and retain original source where available.
capabilities.week_later: One remembered phrase or share action; do not force a separate screenshot management workflow.
capabilities.boundary: No automatic silent uploads; protected content and current-screen capture may be restricted; image model input/return must be tested.

capabilities.name: Capture passage or page
capabilities.why: Text, source URL, page number and quote preserve far more useful context than a bare screenshot.
mechanisms: Userscript selection and DOM extraction
Share sheet JavaScript with active Safari page
Kami adapter for document/page anchors
capabilities.acceptance: Capture a selected paragraph from Wikipedia and a real book passage from Kami; reopen the exact source or documented fallback.
capabilities.week_later: Same Capture/Ask verb regardless of source.
capabilities.boundary: Selection in PDFs or canvases is not guaranteed accessible as DOM text; use existing supported adapter or explicit image.

capabilities.name: Hands-free native control
capabilities.why: Eliminate routine touch interactions without writing an accessibility clone.
mechanisms: iPad Voice Control named elements, numbered overlays and custom gestures
Custom command or Vocal Shortcut for named workflows
capabilities.acceptance: Navigate an actual Safari page and native app without touch; record which controls fail.
capabilities.week_later: Use existing Apple vocabulary; only add custom phrases that recur.
capabilities.boundary: Voice Control dictation modes differ from ordinary dictation; availability varies by OS/language; cannot arbitrarily inspect other apps.

capabilities.name: Semantic DOM control
capabilities.why: Browser commands should reference actual page semantics rather than brittle coordinates; local execution should be fast and independent of inference.
mechanisms: Userscript accessible names, roles, stable site adapters and visible target IDs
Native voice control can tap the pill; dictate a command or use a named custom shortcut
Deterministic routing first
capabilities.acceptance: On GitHub and Kami, issue three spoken commands, verify actual resulting page states; handle ambiguous targets by asking which one, never click blindly.
capabilities.week_later: One Command entry; show available verbs and contextual actions; no memorized selector syntax.
capabilities.boundary: Voice-to-userscript bridge must be proved. Synthetic clicks may fail for trusted gestures, cross-origin frames or canvas; use native control fallback.

capabilities.name: Contextual AI request
capabilities.why: Make intelligence callable without reconstructing page context or switching research modes.
mechanisms: Explicit ChatGPT/Gemini handoff initially
Shortcuts Use Model or eligible official subscription transport
Separate API if useful
capabilities.acceptance: Ask a novel question about a real article and receive a relevant response, distinguishing manual handoff from automatic same-page return.
capabilities.week_later: Ask is the default entry; provider remembered but visible; same interaction across sites.
capabilities.boundary: Existing subscriptions do not automatically grant API access; no scraping or unauthorized consumer automation.

capabilities.name: AI-proposed browser operations
intentions: Find the relevant implementation and open it
Take me to the underlying mechanism
capabilities.why: Higher-level goals map to a sequence of low-level operations, after local command coverage is established.
mechanisms: Bounded action list from supported model; validate against current visible targets; local executor
capabilities.acceptance: Open the correct relevant link on a real unfamiliar page after inspecting a model-proposed action; refuse stale or ambiguous targets.
capabilities.week_later: Use ordinary language; preview consequential actions rather than exposing programming vocabulary.
capabilities.boundary: No arbitrary code from model or page; no automatic purchases, messages, permission changes or other consequential actions.

capabilities.name: Capture an idea, question or resource
capabilities.why: Many good questions disappear because categorization or repository navigation interrupts the encounter.
mechanisms: One local JSON inbox with stable ID, source, capture time, kind and optional note
Existing Kami/FKEN adapters; explicit review before canonical commit
capabilities.acceptance: Capture one question, one paper and one repo from different sources; recover all later with their original provenance.
capabilities.week_later: One Save entry, deferred classification; never require choosing a folder first.
capabilities.boundary: No duplication of canonical research; private captures stay local until reviewed.

capabilities.name: Anchor an insight to a book
intentions: Attach this thought to the passage
Add a question to this page
capabilities.why: Kami already provides source-linked reading and durable question/insight records; reuse that capability.
mechanisms: Existing Kami Reading Companion and supported page/annotation mechanisms
Dictation and explicit capture confirmation
capabilities.acceptance: Save a real question with a passage/page and reopen the original book after reload; verify annotation survives.
capabilities.week_later: Keep direct highlight and note actions; no generic assistant ceremony for simple annotations.
capabilities.boundary: Existing code is precedent, not evidence the new iPad workflow works; do not export credentials.

capabilities.name: Resume investigation
capabilities.why: Avoid reconstructing investigation state across chats, books and repositories; preserve trajectories not just summaries.
mechanisms: Small local working-context pointer to canonical investigation/question/source IDs
Existing RSM Tree Viewer and Kami/Drive links
capabilities.acceptance: After a day, recover one real research branch, last source, unresolved question and next action without searching history.
capabilities.week_later: Resume shows current work and recent contexts; no exact ID memorization.
capabilities.boundary: Do not clone canonical investigation data or claim private chat history access.

capabilities.name: Explore a domain or unfamiliar concept
intentions: Show me projects that use this
capabilities.why: FKEN connects vocabulary, questions, working projects, axioms and practical probes; quick routing supports opportunistic learning.
mechanisms: Existing RSM Tree Viewer with scoped domain/query where supported
FKEN glossary, domain JSON and project links
Search fallback
capabilities.acceptance: Start from an unfamiliar term in a paper; find relevant FKEN concept or domain, real implementation and a practical probe.
capabilities.week_later: A single Explore action, not separate launchers for each dataset.
capabilities.boundary: Viewer query parameters and private access must be checked; unknown terms should surface absence rather than fabricated links.

capabilities.name: Reconcile captures into knowledge
capabilities.why: Fast capture and deliberate synthesis are different cognitive modes; batch organization prevents live interruption.
mechanisms: Local inbox to reviewable JSON patch or prompt
Agent-assisted deduplication, canonical stable IDs and source links
capabilities.acceptance: Review a small real mixed capture batch; merge two related items without losing provenance; leave unresolved items recoverable.
capabilities.week_later: One review queue, not a separate tagging ritual per capture.
capabilities.boundary: Human reviews canonical writes; no silent destructive merges or public upload.

capabilities.name: Local shell and file transformations
capabilities.why: iSH is already installed; ordinary git, jq, grep, curl and Python can remove repetitive file/JSON operations without an AI request.
mechanisms: iSH Alpine x86 emulation; install needed packages via apk
Files app / explicit import-export or user-selected mount
capabilities.acceptance: On target iPad clone a public project, transform a real investigation JSON and reopen result in Files; measure setup friction.
capabilities.week_later: Use a small named set of reviewed jobs; retain terminal for arbitrary explicit commands.
capabilities.boundary: iSH does not grant native iPad UI access; package compatibility and file-provider paths require verification.

capabilities.name: Safari/Shortcuts to iSH
capabilities.why: A real local computation provider could support the pill without a deployed backend.
mechanisms: Loopback HTTP canary while iSH foreground or split screen
Explicit file exchange as suspension-tolerant alternative
capabilities.acceptance: From Safari or Shortcuts, send a nonce-bearing real JSON job to local iSH, return validated result, then repeat after app switch; compare file handoff.
capabilities.week_later: Invoke from Ask/Run without managing a server; only promote if startup and recovery are tolerable.
capabilities.boundary: No assumption of persistent daemon, direct shortcut shell execution or Safari localhost cross-origin access. Bind loopback only, authenticate, allowlist operations; never execute arbitrary model-generated shell.

capabilities.name: Run work on available compute
capabilities.why: Local emulation is useful for small jobs; existing remote systems can do heavier work and leave durable artifacts.
mechanisms: Existing Logical Cloud/Fire task contracts and authorized SSH or GitHub Actions
Explicit job request with result link
capabilities.acceptance: Submit one real existing project's reproducible build or analysis, retrieve artifact/result and distinguish queued/running/completed.
capabilities.week_later: One Run action; provider selection only when material.
capabilities.boundary: No new always-on service assumed; authenticated authorized resources only.

capabilities.name: Accelerated code and Shortcut delivery
capabilities.why: The feedback loop from agent commit to running iPad behavior is itself a frequent workflow.
mechanisms: Git pull or raw .user.js install via Userscripts
Cherri source-to-Shortcut compilation and supported signing/import
capabilities.acceptance: Update a versioned real script, verify visible version and behavior, roll back; separately prove one Cherri Shortcut imports and runs.
capabilities.week_later: One update path and one rollback; no repeated manual block construction when avoidable.
capabilities.boundary: Userscripts popup reload and Shortcut signing may require user gestures; never auto-install unreviewed code.

capabilities.name: Curated ambient intelligence
intentions: Give me something worth thinking about
capabilities.why: Use otherwise idle attention for novel questions, useful discoveries and unresolved ideas without notification overload.
mechanisms: Explicit context snapshot; model selects one item
Scriptable/native image rendering; widget or wallpaper; time/Focus automation after manual test
capabilities.acceptance: Display one genuine relevant question on the actual iPad widget or wallpaper, then test scheduled refresh and usefulness over a week.
capabilities.week_later: One refresh control; at most a few high-value items, quiet by default.
capabilities.boundary: No arbitrary custom screensaver or guaranteed refresh; do not expose sensitive data on lock screen.

capabilities.name: Selective research briefing
capabilities.why: Useful only if it reduces repeated checking and adds intellectual variance rather than generic summaries.
mechanisms: Explicit project pointers and public source changes; summarize with source links; native speech or widget
capabilities.acceptance: Generate a briefing from actual selected work and discoveries; after a week compare whether it changed a question or action.
capabilities.week_later: Opt-in cadence; skip when nothing consequential; one place to find it.
capabilities.boundary: No continuous device surveillance or assumption of autonomous personal chat access.

capabilities.name: What's happening / stop / copy report
capabilities.why: A fast workflow is only fast if failures don't require reconstructing implementation details.
mechanisms: Single visible status, stop, recent stage history, sanitized report
Existing Microsoft/LabX lifecycle patterns
capabilities.acceptance: Induce realistic failure (tab switch, unavailable provider or stale target), see correct status and export sufficient diagnostic details without developer tools.
capabilities.week_later: Same Details/Stop labels across workflows; ordinary UI remains small.
capabilities.boundary: Never include tokens, full screenshots, private text or secrets by default; no hidden retries.

workflows.example: See a circuit diagram in Kami -> screenshot or passage -> ask why -> save a source-linked question -> resume later
Speak open commit history -> deterministic DOM route -> read changes -> ask about a file -> navigate to it
Encounter an unfamiliar mechanism -> capture term/source -> open domain landscape -> choose a skill probe -> reconcile discovery
Screenshot real failure -> copy diagnostics -> ask for interpretation -> validate JSON/patch in iSH -> run authorized build -> inspect result
Recover selected unresolved research -> choose one valuable question -> render to widget/wallpaper -> reopen its source

next_experiments: Preserve existing AssistiveTouch double tap; manually test screenshot+question handoff.
Enable Voice Control and test known native commands; then test dictation to a minimal DOM pill on GitHub/Kami.
Test inference transport separately from browser execution.
Use iSH for a real JSON operation, then a short loopback request and app-switch recovery test only if valuable.
Capture and resume one real Kami/FKEN investigation before inventing a new state system.

observations.evidence: User reports screenshotting is linked to double tapping the accessibility virtual button.
observations.scope: User-reported existing baseline; no direct device inspection.
Installation reported; shell commands and integration not tested.

thoughts: Screenshots are a universal visual context channel; DOM is a semantic context and execution channel. Neither subsumes the other.
The common unit of acceleration is the transition from an encounter to a useful next state, not a shortcut action.
Fast capture and slow reconciliation should be separate; the human should not classify every idea at the instant of discovery.
A local computation provider can be useful even if iPadOS never permits dependable background execution.
